The trust ladder R6 sells is an attacker-typed string; invariant 2 (`authored_sha256`) is set membership over a list the attacker also supplies, so declaring `[]` disarms it.
attacks.name: Fully self-minted manifest: attacker supplies the receipt bytes, declares trust rung L2, spoofs the harness name, and omits `digest` entirely so integrity is never checked
attacks.why: load_sidecar checks the manifest is a dict with a known spec, a dict-of-dicts `receipts` and a list-of-strings `authored_sha256` — every field that decides trust (`harness`, `rung`, `kind_of_source`, `complete`, `bytes`) is unchecked. The builder computes the digest with rung "L1", then ships rung "L2" with that same digest; `intact()` still passes and every span's provenance prints rung L2. attacks.goal: Break the parrhesia discipline: the content-addressed verdict receipt stops being re-derivable. `Manifest.from_dict` passes `d.get("minted_at")` = None into `__init__`, which substitutes `_now()` at second resolution, so `manifest_digest` — and therefore the whole receipt digest — changes between two verifications a second apart. attacks.name: Omit `minted_at` — a field load_sidecar never requires — and the verdict receipt's manifest_digest becomes a function of the wall clock
attacks.why: `self.minted_at = minted_at or _now()` and `_now()` returns `datetime.now(utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")`. `core()` puts `minted_at` in the digested body. With `digest` also omitted, `intact()` is True so the span still HELDs — the document verifies, but its receipt carries a manifest_digest that will not reproduce. Verifying twice across a second boundary yields two different receipt digests for identical input bytes, which is exactly the property the receipt claims. The defect is silent: no reason code exists for "the manifest supplied no mint time and I invented one".

The entry keyed `r1` self-identifies as `"id": "r9"` and carries {"n": 7}; the entry keyed `r9` self-identifies as `"id": "r1"` and carries {"n": 99}. `_resolve` keys on the dict key and never compares it to the entry's `id`, so `r1#/n` HELDs against 7 while an auditor reading the manifest by `id` reads 99. There is no length bound and no `_safe_text` on this path, unlike the detail strings the module deliberately sanitises. verify_receipt re-feeds `doc.get("name", "")` back into verify, so the forged name is exactly what makes the digest match on re-derivation. The one mitigation is accidental: the CLI's verify path overrides with `name=Path(a.target).name` (line 1903), so this bites the library API and every non-CLI consumer, not `python -m styxx.sworn verify`.

attacks.goal: Two sidecars with byte-identical text and therefore identical document.sha256 (and identical canonical_sha256 in both receipts) that swear the same number to DIFFERENT receipts and produce different rendered documents and different receipt digests. The digest a reader would cite as 'this is that document' does not determine what was sworn, who it was sworn to, or what bytes get published — text is digested, the span table and manifest are not.
attacks.name: Same text, same document.sha256, a different oath — one digest, two contradictory receipts
attacks.why: document.sha256 is `_sha256(text)` and text alone; the span table, the receipt strings, the kinds, the manifest and the commit are all outside it. Any self-consistent span table over the same text renders and re-scans cleanly, so the honest sidecar (receipt path:runs/audit.json#/n) and this one (path:attacker/reroute.json#/n) both verify with the same document.sha256 and the same receipt-core canonical_sha256 while pointing the same sentence at different evidence. Re-pointing a span to a file the attacker controls is a one-field edit that the digest was supposed to make impossible and does not.

attacks.name: Digest an innocent already-published file, then invent oaths over it
attacks.why: load_sidecar never scans text, so it cannot tell an unsworn published file from a canonical form that was ever sworn — text is just a string that hashes right. Nothing in the sidecar records the digest of render(sidecar), so the only digest present is the one matching the innocent file. A recipient at stop 2 who publishes render(sidecar) publishes bytes whose sha256 appears nowhere in the object they validated; a recipient who instead copies the human-readable `text` field out publishes bytes that match document.sha256 exactly and carry no declarations at all (UNSWORN). One sidecar, two documents, and the digest endorses the wrong one.

attacks.name: Fence swallows the rendered tags: text hashes correctly, the rendered document's canon is different bytes
attacks.why: load_sidecar validates offsets only as an ordered non-overlapping range on UTF-8 boundaries — it has no idea the range is inside a fenced region, because it never lexes text. render() inserts blindly. At stop 3 this dies, but on `re-scanning the rendered sidecar does not reproduce its spans` (seen=[] vs want=[one span]) — a span-table check, not a digest check. Nothing anywhere compares the sidecar's document.sha256 against `_sha256(sc["canonical"])`, which verify() computes and writes into the receipt one line later; the two digests are allowed to disagree silently. from styxx.sworn import Manifest
sha = lambda b: hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()

def _wrap(pieces, meta):
    text = "".join(pieces); offs = []; pos = 0
    for p in pieces:
        n = len(p.encode("utf-8")); offs.append((pos, pos + n)); pos += n
    return text, [{"start": offs[i][0], "end": offs[i][1], "receipt": r, "kind": k}
                  for (i, r, k) in meta]

# out/agent_metrics.json is a byte-object the agent produced this turn. The harness
# recorded it, honestly, in authored_sha256. _resolve consults that list ONLY on the
# rn branch; the path: branch never looks at it.
mine = b'{"precision": 0.9500}\n'
m = Manifest(harness="acme-harness", turn="t1",
             minted_at="2026-09-05T00:00:00Z", rung="L2")
m.authored_sha256 = [sha(mine)]

text, spans = _wrap(
    ["Precision on the held-out set was ", "0.95", ".\n"],
    [(1, "path:out/agent_metrics.json#/precision", "numeric")])
return {"spec": "sworn/0.1", "commit": "c" * 40,
        "document": {"name": "RESULT.md", "sha256": sha(text.encode("utf-8"))},
        "text": text, "spans": spans, "manifest": m.to_dict()}
attacks.goal: Swear a number against a JSON file the agent wrote itself, while the SAME sidecar's manifest honestly records that file's digest in authored_sha256 — the exact set-membership test invariant 2 was reduced to — and get HELD.
attacks.name: authored_sha256 is dead on `path:` — the sidecar carries the proof of its own authorship and HELDs anyway
attacks.why: The cleanest 'a check on one field is undermined by a value in another' in the module: the refusal `sha in manifest.authored_sha256 -> receipt_author_minted` and the digest that would trigger it are both present in this one sidecar, three keys apart, and the receipt form decides they never meet. Executed: HELD, rungs {'committed': 1}, provenance note 'committed object at cccc…; authorship unchecked'. The v0.1 battery's A5 knows a committed receipt can be author-written and answers it by PRINTING that authorship was unchecked; what nobody noticed is that the verifier is not merely unable to check — it is holding the answer and not reading it. A one-line fix exists (`or (manifest and sha in manifest.authored_sha256)` on the tree branch) and no attacker asked for it, because all six were reading the rn branch.

attacks.goal: HELD a 58-byte quote against a sentence the agent wrote into its own draft file, using no manifest at all, and leave a verdict receipt from which no reader can locate the object that satisfied the oath.
attacks.name: pathless prereg: content-address an author-committed draft, and the verdict receipt records no path
attacks.why: Executed: HELD, rungs {'committed': 1}, detail {needle_bytes: 58, haystack_bytes: 63, occurrences: 1}. Two properties nobody probed. First, prereg: needs neither a manifest nor a path — the whole channel is a content-addressed grep over the tree, so an agent that can write any file anywhere in the repo can mint the haystack for any quote or numeric oath, and A5's 'authorship unchecked' disclosure applies without anyone having chosen a path to disclose. Second, the verdict receipt for a prereg span records provenance {form: 'prereg', note: 'committed object at <commit>; authorship unchecked'} and resolved_sha256 == the digest the AUTHOR supplied: no path, no object name, nothing a reader can look up. The receipt is content-addressed and re-derivable, and still tells you nothing about where the bytes were.

attacks.goal: Swear 0.95 against line 12 of a CHANGELOG — a file that is not JSON, was never a capture, and whose one numeric line the author wrote.
attacks.name: line-anchored numeric turns any committed text file into a numeric receipt
attacks.why: Executed: HELD, rungs {'committed': 1}, detail receipt '0.9500'. The DECISIONS entry says 'a line-anchored slice must itself be one JSON number' — a constraint on the LINE, not on the file, so the anchor promotes any committed text file containing a bare-number line into a numeric evidence source. Chain it with the previous attack (the path: branch never consults authored_sha256) and the agent's own changelog line becomes a 'committed' receipt for whatever number it wants. The combination is what earns the row: the fragment grammar (unattacked), the tree branch's missing authorship check (unattacked), and the rungs histogram filing the result under the reassuring key 'committed', in the same headline position where L1 and L2 appear.

produced: six attackers, one per surface, plus an adversary asked to find what they left alone and to look for interactions BETWEEN surfaces. Every prediction was written before any attack was executed (G-P).

unattacked_after_the_adversary.area: The evidence channel — what the receipt attribute RESOLVES TO, and whether it resolves at all
unattacked_after_the_adversary.why_it_matters: All six attackers attacked what the sidecar SAYS (its text, its offsets, its attribute bytes, its manifest fields, its identity fields). Nobody attacked what the sidecar POINTS AT. The receipt string is the only field in the format that selects which bytes the verifier compares against, and load_sidecar validates it with exactly one regex — _ATTR_VALUE, which only asks 'can the inline tag grammar carry these characters'. Nothing at stop 1 or stop 2 looks at the receipt's grammar, its form (rn / path: / prereg:), or its fragment. Every semantic consequence of that string is deferred to _parse_receipt and _resolve at stop 3, where it is never compared against anything the sidecar already committed to.

unattacked_after_the_adversary.area: UNRESOLVED is not FAILED: document_verdict is SWORN-HELD whenever counts['FAILED'] == 0 and counts['MALFORMED'] == 0, however many spans went UNRESOLVED
unattacked_after_the_adversary.why_it_matters: The author cannot choose what the receipt says — but the author CAN choose whether a receipt is consulted at all, and an unconsulted receipt costs nothing. Three independent sidecar-owned levers each turn spans UNRESOLVED en masse without touching text, offsets, digests or attribute validity: commit:null (no_commit), a reserved rung string (rung_unknown, which fires before the receipt id is even looked up), and an rN id absent from the manifest (manifest_id_missing). A document whose every oath is wrong prints SWORN-HELD. The manifest attacker touched one instance of this via an empty receipts dict, framed as a digest problem; the lattice itself was never the target.

unattacked_after_the_adversary.area: The `#` fragment grammar — JSON pointers and line anchors on the receipt
unattacked_after_the_adversary.why_it_matters: The attributes surface attacked bytes inside the attribute (surrogates, NUL, ANSI, zero-width) but never the attribute's own grammar. `#/pointer` and `#Ln-Lm` re-aim the comparison at a sub-object the reader cannot see from the tag, and both of them SWITCH OFF the v0.2 R3 short_needle floor: _check_quote exempts a pointer leaf by early return and exempts any line slice via `if res['slice'] is None and len(needle) < SHORT_NEEDLE_BYTES`. A check on the span-text field is disabled by a value in the receipt field. The exemption's stated justification ('the author narrowed the haystack by naming it') is enforced nowhere: `#L1-L400` narrows nothing. And JSON pointer's `~1` escape lets one tag mean two different leaves to a machine and to a human.

unattacked_after_the_adversary.area: `path:` and `prereg:` — the two receipt forms where invariant 2 has no teeth and `complete` is hard-coded
unattacked_after_the_adversary.why_it_matters: In _resolve, the author-minted refusal (`kos in SOURCE_KINDS_AUTHOR or sha in manifest.authored_sha256` -> receipt_author_minted) exists ONLY on the rn branch. The tree branch never consults manifest.authored_sha256 — not even when the sidecar's OWN manifest, three keys away, records that exact digest as agent-authored. The tree branch also sets `complete = True` unconditionally, which is the precondition the strongest verdict in the format (`absent`) turns on. Two of the three evidence channels answer 'the author could not have written these bytes' with a hard-coded yes. Every manifest attack in the battery was aimed at the one channel that actually checks.

unattacked_after_the_adversary.area: `commit` as an evidence switch rather than an identity field
unattacked_after_the_adversary.why_it_matters: The digest_binding attackers treated commit as part of the document's identity (transplant it, forge it, set it to the text's own sha). It is also the sole input to `tree.commit = commit` in verify(), i.e. the switch that decides whether the entire tree channel can see anything at all. commit:null is a legal, load_sidecar-approved, digest-consistent value that silently blinds every path: and prereg: span in the document at once — no forgery required, nothing detectable in the bytes.

unattacked_after_the_adversary.area: The numeric comparison's precision is set by the span's own printed text
unattacked_after_the_adversary.why_it_matters: _check_numeric quantizes the RECEIPT to `frac`, the number of fractional digits the AUTHOR printed, with ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Span text and receipt are separately attacker-chosen and load_sidecar cross-checks neither. Printing zero fractional digits rounds the receipt's entire value away: a leaf of 0.4211 canonicalizes to '0'. The DECISIONS block discloses the rounding rule; no attacker in this battery, and no row in the frozen v0.1 twelve-way battery, tried driving it. It needs no malformed anything, a genuinely harness-minted L2 receipt, and it converts a real 0.4211 into a sworn, HELD 0.

unattacked_after_the_adversary.area: What the verdict receipt records about WHERE evidence came from
unattacked_after_the_adversary.why_it_matters: For prereg:, provenance is `{form: 'prereg', note: 'committed object at <sha>; authorship unchecked'}` and resolved_sha256 is the digest the author supplied. No path is recorded anywhere, because find_sha256 searches the whole tree by content — a reader holding the receipt cannot locate the object that satisfied the oath. Separately, the `rungs` histogram buckets every tree-resolved span under the key `committed`, which sits in the headline beside L1/L2 and reads as a rung. It is not one; it is the bucket for the two forms with no authorship check.
